subject: Orchard Care SSQ: questions on dataflow, KMS custody, and subprocessors
messages:
From: Michael Tanaka <m.tanaka@orchardcare.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: security@orchardcare.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orchard Care SSQ v1 — clarifications on PII flow and subprocessors

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our standard privacy/security questionnaire (SSQ) — I'm attaching v1 with inline sections we flagged as 'clarify'. Our immediate asks:

- Can you confirm which Redwood subprocessors handle raw customer inputs (text) vs. derived telemetry? We need an explicit list and locations.
- For PII fields we mark as 'sensitive' (names, contact, health notes), can you confirm if Redwood's default proxy retains any raw tokens beyond KV cache lifetimes and whether that data can be exported?
- KMS custody: do you support customer-managed keys for model artifacts and token logs? If yes, what evidence can you provide (attestation or architecture diagram)?
- Audit logs: we require a 12-month exportable audit trail for token-level access. Is that available? Format?

I've attached Orchard_SSQ_v1.pdf and a redacted dataflow sketch (for context). We're hoping to close security review this month so any short answers + artifacts you can share are helpful.

Thanks,
Michael Tanaka
Head of Privacy
Orchard Care
security@orchardcare.com

Attachment: Orchard_SSQ_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Michael Tanaka <m.tanaka@orchardcare.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchard Care SSQ v1 — clarifications on PII flow and subprocessors

Hi Michael — thanks for the file and the clear list. Looping in Lauren (security), Karthik (platform), and Jordan (legal) to address each ask. High-level responses follow — we can provide artifacts & a short call Friday if useful.

1) Subprocessor list by data role: we maintain a published subprocessor roster; for request scope we will produce a mapping that differentiates: ingestion/edge proxies, telemetry/observability, and storage/backups. Karthik, can you attach the current roster slice for Orchard?

2) Raw tokens retention: Redwood's serving runtime keeps KV cache in-memory per-request and persists only operational telemetry; by default we do NOT write raw input tokens to long-term storage. We do maintain transient logs for debugging which are configurable/elidable per-customer. Lauren — I'll let you add the compliance note here about retention options and exportability.

3) Customer-managed keys: We support KMS integration (customer-managed keys) for exportable artifacts and for datastore encryption at rest in Private deployments. For Hosted accounts we provide a bring-your-own-KMS option on our Dedicated plan — Jordan will share the attestation language we can include in the DPA annex.

4) Audit logs: We can export token-level access logs for 12 months as a downloadable parquet/CSV; format includes timestamp, request_id, model, route, and an index pointer (not raw tokens unless customer enables verbose capture). We'll produce a sample extract.

Next steps: Karthik to attach the subprocessor extract and the dataflow diagram revision; Lauren to provide a short bullet list on retention controls and certs; Jordan to comment on DPA language for BYOK. If you're available Friday 10–11am PT we can review artifacts.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_dataflow_diagram_v2.png (image/png)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Michael Tanaka <m.tanaka@orchardcare.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchard Care SSQ v1 — clarifications on PII flow and subprocessors

Hi all — attaching the subprocessor-role extract and a KMS custody matrix. Short notes:

- Subprocessors handling raw inputs: edge-proxy providers (us-east edge pool), our streaming layer (Redwood-servlet), and optional managed vector-store partner for embeddings (listed in extract). Locations: primary US regions (us-west-2, us-east-1); EU-only tenancy available for Private deployments.
- Telemetry/observability: hosted telemetry is serviced by our observability stack partner; telemetry is pseudonymized by default (request_id keyed) and can be disabled.
- KV cache behavior: KV cache is ephemeral and kept in GPU RAM for inference; we do not persist KV cache to disk in normal operation.

Attachments included: kms-custody-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet) — this maps options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (BYOK, HSM integration, attestation artifacts). Also attaching a slightly updated dataflow diagram with the edge/ingest boundary annotated.

Happy to walk through Friday.

—Karthik Iyer
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: kms-custody-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Michael Tanaka <m.tanaka@orchardcare.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchard Care SSQ v1 — clarifications on PII flow and subprocessors

Michael — quick compliance bullet answers as promised.

- Retention: By default, Redwood retains operational telemetry (no raw tokens) for 90 days. Customers on Dedicated or Private plans can configure a 12-month audit export for request-level metadata. Raw token capture is explicit and opt-in; we will not capture raw PII tokens unless customer toggles verbose capture in configuration.

- Export format: Audit exports are available as compressed parquet/CSV. We will provide a sample export schema and a one-off extract for Orchard to validate.

- KMS & attestation: For Dedicated/DPA customers we support BYOK (Cloud KMS) and HSM-backed key stores; we will provide a key-custody attestation document and a short architecture diagram showing key flow. For Hosted customers we offer encrypted-at-rest with Redwood-managed keys; migration to BYOK is available during onboarding.

- Subprocessors: We publish a live subprocessor roster and provide a snapshot on request. Any subprocessor with access to plaintext is highlighted in the roster; we run contractual flow-downs and periodic reassessments.

Next steps: Marissa will share links to the two artifacts Karthik uploaded and a sample audit export schema. If Orchard wants, we can schedule the Friday 10am PT call to go over the sample artifacts and draft DPA annex language.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
